findings.title: Committed editor backup `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts-E` is stale dead code
findings.description: The diff adds a new 146-line file that is a byte-for-byte copy of the *pre-change* `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts` (blob `e6539010`). It calls `createContextPipeline(FIXTURE_PROJECT_PATH)` with the now-required options argument omitted at lines 29, 35, 59, 99, 119 and 141, so it would fail if it were ever executed. It is invisible to every gate: `packages/core/vitest.config.ts:5` only matches `tests/**/*.{test,spec}.{js,mjs,cjs,ts,mts,cts}` (the `-E` suffix does not match), `packages/core/tsconfig.json:19` includes only `src/**/*`, and `eslint.config.mjs:9` ignores `**/tests/**` and matches only `*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}`. `.gitignore` has no `-E` rule, so this backup is now tracked. Delete it.

findings.title: `template_preview`'s read-only contract is only partially honored by the new `read-only` mode
findings.description: The added `'read-only'` argument and its comment invoke `template_preview`'s "without side effects" contract, but the option only suppresses the adoption-state write inside `createContextPipeline`. `template_preview` reaches the shared `generateContext` helper (`packages/mcp-server/src/tools/contextTools.ts#generateContext`), which unconditionally calls `ensureGuideForProject(workingCopy.projectPath!)`; that calls `GuideManager.ensureCheckout()`, and for an uninitialized submodule `packages/core/src/guides/GuideManager.ts:186-215` runs `initGuideCheckout()` → `SubmoduleStrategy.init()`, i.e. checks out files into the checkout. The tool is registered with `readOnlyHint: true` and described as "without modifying the stored project or triggering any side effects". This behavior predates the diff, but the new option/comment now implies the tool is fully side-effect-free; narrow the claim or skip guide readiness on the `read-only` path. The new mock-based test at `packages/mcp-server/tests/contextTools.test.ts:371-377` only asserts the factory argument, so it cannot catch this.

findings.title: New parity test's cleanup hooks can mask the real failure
findings.description: `fixtureEnv`, `ctx`, `client` and `checkout` are uninitialized module-level `let`s (lines 31-34), populated only in `beforeAll` and inside the single `it`. `afterAll` dereferences `ctx.cleanup()` and `fixtureEnv.cleanup()` unconditionally, and `afterEach` passes `checkout` straight to `fs.rmSync`. If `setupFixtureEnv()`, `createIntegrationClient()`, or `createBrownfieldCheckout()` throws, the hooks throw a `TypeError` on `undefined` and hide the root cause; `checkout` is also never reset between tests (which matters if this file grows more cases). Guard both hooks (`if (ctx)`, `if (fixtureEnv)`, `if (checkout)`) and clear `checkout` after removal, following the pattern in `packages/core/tests/adoption/adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts`, which restores `originalEnv` defensively.

findings.title: New required mode parameter keeps piling onto positional signatures
findings.description: `generateContext` now takes five positional parameters with the new required `adoptionStateWrites` inserted before three optional ones, so both call sites (`packages/mcp-server/src/tools/contextTools.ts:202` and `:266`) must spell out long positional lists. The same pattern is extended in `packages/core/src/services/ContextIntegrator.ts:84-93`, whose constructor now has seven positional parameters; the new adoption tests have to pass `null, null, null` placeholders (`packages/core/tests/services/ContextIntegrator.test.ts:384`). The TypeScript rules prefer named parameters via object destructuring for functions with 3+ parameters. An options object for the adoption mode/resolver would make the new boundary self-documenting and avoid future placeholder churn.
